title: Self-Confirming Equilibrium under Model Misspecification
abstract: arXiv:2610.35692v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study the steady states of games played recurrently within large anonymous populations of players who receive partial ex-post feedback about the play of their opponents. Departing from the classical Bayesian account, players do not trust their conjectures as a correct description of the strategic environment but consider them as approximations of a reality that is only partially modeled and partially observed. We introduce games with feedback and uncertainty attitudes, in which the normal-form structure is enriched with a profile of feedback functions and, for each player, a preference functional that encodes aversion to misspecification and to ambiguity. The induced misspecification sensitive criterion contains the variational, maxmin, and smooth-ambiguity evaluations as special cases and collapses to expected utility when beliefs are unambiguous and the player is neutral to misspecification. translated_title: 模型误设下的自我确认均衡
translated_abstract: 我们研究在大型匿名玩家群体中反复进行的博弈的稳态，其中玩家关于对手行为的事后反馈是不完全的。与经典的贝叶斯框架不同，玩家并不信任自己的猜想是对策略环境的正确描述，而是将其视为对一个仅被部分建模、部分观察到的现实的近似。我们引入了带有反馈与不确定性态度的博弈，其中标准式结构通过一组成员反馈函数得到扩展，并为每个玩家定义了一个偏好泛函，用以刻画其对模型误设和模糊性的厌恶。由此产生的对误设敏感的决策准则将变分偏好、最大最小偏好和光滑模糊性偏好评估作为特例包含在内，并且当信念无模糊且玩家对误设中性时，该准则退化为期望效用。相应的稳态概念……（原文在此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出在玩家只能获得部分反馈且对模型误设与模糊性持厌恶态度的环境下研究博弈的稳态，将变分、最大最小与光滑模糊性偏好统一纳入自我确认均衡的框架之中。
en_tdlr: This paper studies steady states of recurrently played games under partial feedback and aversion to model misspecification and ambiguity, unifying variational, maxmin, and smooth-ambiguity preferences within a self-confirming equilibrium framework.
